findings.title: Negative offset slicing of a Django QuerySet raises AssertionError
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and the incoming cursor has a negative offset (which any client can supply via a cursor string like `0:-5:0`, parsed by Cursor.from_string), the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. The comment claims 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', but this is false: Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. Since the audit log endpoint passes `enable_advanced_features=True` for superusers/admins, any such user supplying a negative-offset cursor gets a 500 instead of a BadPaginationError or a clamped offset.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator key handling is numeric but the endpoint orders by datetime
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `int(math.floor(value))` / `math.ceil(value)` on the sort key, which only works for numeric values. The audit logs endpoint uses it with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a datetime object and `math.floor(datetime)` raises a TypeError. The endpoint previously used DateTimePaginator, which converts the datetime to a millisecond timestamp. As written, the 'optimized' path will fail with a 500 on the first page that has results (build_cursor always calls get_item_key). OptimizedCursorPaginator needs the DateTimePaginator key conversion (or should subclass it).

findings.title: organization_context.member can be None for superusers
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `.member` unconditionally via the `or` chain — actually Python short-circuits when is_superuser is True, but a non-superuser whose RpcUserOrganizationContext has `member=None` (e.g. access via org auth token or other non-member paths that this endpoint permits through OrganizationAuditPermission) will hit `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'` and get a 500 on every request to this endpoint, even when not requesting optimized pagination. Guard with `organization_context.member is not None and organization_context.member.has_global_access`.

findings.title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative offsets, changing prev-cursor semantics
findings.body: The change in BasePaginator.get_result replaces `results = queryset[offset:stop]` with `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For non-prev cursors, a negative offset was previously impossible to reach successfully (Django would raise), so clamping changes behavior silently for all users of Paginator/DateTimePaginator codebase-wide: a client-supplied negative-offset cursor that used to fail loudly now returns the first page as if offset were 0, while the cursor arithmetic later (`_build_next_values` uses the raw `cursor.offset`) still computes next offsets from the original negative offset, producing inconsistent cursors. If clamping is intended, it should be applied uniformly (and probably rejected with BadPaginationError instead), not papered over only in the slice.

findings.title: enable_advanced_features passed through self.paginate may not reach the paginator
findings.body: The endpoint calls `self.paginate(..., paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator, ..., enable_advanced_features=True)`. Sentry's base `Endpoint.paginate` only forwards a fixed set of arguments when constructing the paginator; arbitrary extra kwargs are not passed to the paginator constructor in the standard implementation. If that is the case here, the paginator will always be constructed with `enable_advanced_features=False` (or paginate will raise TypeError for the unexpected kwarg), and the new code path is dead. This needs a test verifying the flag actually reaches OptimizedCursorPaginator.

findings.title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized audit log path
findings.body: This PR adds a new paginator (~90 lines) with non-trivial boundary logic (negative offsets, prev-cursor extra-row trimming, cursor building) and a new branch in the audit logs endpoint, but includes no tests. Given that both the datetime key handling and the negative-slice behavior are broken as noted, unit tests covering first-page, next-page, prev-page, and malformed-cursor cases for OptimizedCursorPaginator, plus an endpoint test with optimized_pagination=true, are required before merging.
